business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed with EU-derived commercial and financial regulatory law; no separate sub-state tax authority)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (1962, in force 1966)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, as amended by 2021 protocol)
Luxembourg–China Agreement on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (1994)
EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union — freedom of establishment and free movement of capital
Benelux Convention on Intellectual Property (trademarks and designs)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting participating jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including the Law of 12 July 2013 which introduced the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and the Law of 25 March 2020 and Law of 17 December 2021 amending AML/CFT provisions; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; CSSF Circular 20/735 on AML/CFT risk factors; CSSF Circular 23/782 on prudential expectations for domiciliation agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association of the SCSp (contrat de société / statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public (notaire) registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable (domestic Luxembourg notarial act); lodged directly with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) by the notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each general partner, limited partner, and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry, police, or consular authority of the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuing state is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and extract of beneficial owners of any corporate partner or shareholder resident outside Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or competent commercial register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states) and sworn translation into French, German, or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each partner and UBO (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy or apostilled copy; accepted by the notary and the domiciliation agent as part of the KYC file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of funds and source of wealth statement, including banking reference letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating regulated bank or wealth-management institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or notarized banking reference; subject to suspicious-transaction review by the Luxembourg notary and the payment processor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation of all non-French, non-German, or non-English corporate and KYC documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator admitted in Luxembourg or an officially certified translator in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's seal and signature certified by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or the competent court registry; where required, apostille on the translator's certificate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, authorized signatories, and UBOs against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) and CSSF guidance, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and the domestic Luxembourg asset-freezing list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are automatically flagged and subjected to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval, with a 12-month post-cessation cooling-off period. The low-risk classification for ISIC 6201 no-code website subscription activities does not derogate from the mandatory screening duty; transactional monitoring applies to expected payment rails (Stripe Billing and Paddle) and all inbound transfers must be traced to a regulated financial institution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing and reservation portal at lbr.lu / rcs.lu; name reservation is ordinarily executed by the notary public through the LBR online dossier submission service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any Latin-alphabet language; filings with the RCS are accepted in French, German, or Luxembourgish, with the LBR operating database records in French. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the notarial deed. The statutory name of an SCSp must contain the words 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' at the end of the name. The name must be distinctive, not contrary to public policy, and must not mislead as to the legal form or the true activity of the entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg/Luxemburger when used in a manner suggesting state sponsorship
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be renewed by the notary before expiry for successive 60-day periods, provided that the reservation has not lapsed. If the LBR/RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant or notary may request a written statement of reasons from the LBR; a formal administrative review must be filed within 15 days of notification. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may bring summary proceedings (référé) before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg within 30 days of the final administrative refusal, seeking an order that the name be accepted for registration. The court's decision is subject to ordinary appeal under the Luxembourg New Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed and CSSF-supervised domiciliation agent that provides a physical registered-office address in Luxembourg. The SCSp must maintain its central administration, minutes, accounting records, and contract files at that address; a pure mail-forwarding or non-staffed virtual office is not acceptable for substance purposes and would trigger adverse tax and AML findings. For the no-code website builder activity, standard commercially available domiciliation packages are adequate provided the agent performs the mandatory client onboarding and ongoing monitoring duties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a passive SCSp engaged in licensed software-code licensing and subscription collection: estimated probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first 12 months is approximately 5%, rising to 15–20% if the domiciliation agent is selected as a CSSF inspection target, if a tax audit is opened, or if any payment processor flags the merchant account under a sanctions false-positive review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and RCS registration lodging fee (droit de dépôt and RESA publication)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff applied by the LBR fee schedule (circulaire du Ministère de la Justice), current official tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of SCSp articles of association, incl. statutory conflict-of-interest and representation clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif notarial) with market benchmark of EUR 1,800–EUR 2,500 for a standard single-partner SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing analysis and RBE filing declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE unit) plus corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE filing has no direct public fee; professional-service benchmark for UBO structuring and disclosure review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance file preparation, PEP and OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening of all partners and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional benchmark for standard-risk software holding vehicles; includes ongoing monitoring for the first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate, passport, proof-of-address, and banking reference documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministries of foreign affairs or courts of the issuing states and Luxembourg consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Applicable consular tariff and apostille fee schedules abroad; assumed four documents at average USD 85 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of non-French/German/English records into an acceptable filing language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market per-page translation tariff for legal documents (approximately EUR 0.40–EUR 0.80 per line)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service for the first year, including mail handling and statutory records reception
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 1,500–EUR 2,200 per annum for a standard-risk SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Payment processor onboarding assistance for Stripe Billing and Paddle merchant accounts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate counsel and external payment-compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for drafting processor declarations, UBO attestations, and beneficial-ownership documentation for low-risk SaaS merchants

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel advisory for name clearance, rejection-appeal readiness, and commercial substance documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate benchmark (EUR 250–EUR 450 per hour) with fixed-fee engagement cap

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Luxembourg Companies Act), Articles 604-1 to 604-12 (Société en Commandite Spéciale regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); supplemented by the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions and the RCS Regulations of Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic registration dossier (dossier d'immatriculation) filed via the LBR portal, comprising the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société), subscription declaration, and statutory declarations of the general partner and gérant.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, no escrow account, and no bank capital certificate is required for an SCSp; the partners agree freely on their contributions (cash or in kind) in the partnership agreement, and the registered office and contributions must be identified to the RCSL (if requested, evidence of contribution may be required).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous Written Resolution of the Sole General Partner of [SCSp Name] — First Corporate Act. The sole general partner resolves: (1) to ratify the formation of this SCSp under the Law of 10 August 1915; (2) to approve the initial limited partner's subscription of partnership interests and in-cash contribution; (3) to adopt the registered office at [address, L-xxxx Luxembourg]; (4) to appoint [Name] as gérant (managing partner), with sole signature authority, authorised to represent the partnership; and (5) to instruct the gérant to file formation documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to register the partnership for VAT and direct tax references, to complete social security formalities, and to open a professional bank account. All ancillary acts necessary for these mandates are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Partnership Agreement and Appointment of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties acting privately (or before a Luxembourg notary if a notarial deed is chosen); no preliminary government filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the partnership agreement (contrat de société) defining the SCSp corporate name, registered office address in Luxembourg, purpose (ISIC 6201 – no-code application building), capital/contribution schedule, profit sharing, rights of limited partners, and management powers of the general partner. Appoint the gérant, who must accept office and confirm good standing. Ensure original signatures and, if the agreement is executed outside Luxembourg, arrange apostilled or legalized extracts for the RCS record.
required_dossiers: Draft final partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Passport or ID copies of the general partner, limited partner(s), and appointed gérant
Criminal record extract (less than 3 months old) for the general partner and gérant
Sworn statement of acceptance of office by the gérant
Evidence of registered office address (lease contract or landlord consent)
POA if acting by a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel flags defective purpose clauses, amend and re-sign before filing; if a criminal record is adverse, the general partner may be replaced before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration through Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the complete registration dossier on the LBR portal. Include the signed partnership agreement and the RCS-specific declarations (subscription, registered office, appointment of manager). Pay the registration and publication fee of approximately EUR 75 (about USD 81) by card or bank transfer. Once the digital filing is submitted, the RCS analytics department verifies capacity, domiciliation evidence, and the manager's declarations; upon approval an RCS number and the matricule are issued, and the file is transmitted automatically to RESA.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (original scan or notarial deed)
RCS filing declaration (déclaration de souscription)
Acceptance declaration of the gérant
Proof of registered office in Luxembourg (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Identity documents of partners/managers
Criminal record extracts
Evidence of fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), respond with corrected documents within the prescribed deadline (typically 15 days); if the RCS refuses registration, lodge an appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within one month or re-file a rectified dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA Electronic Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes the mandatory incorporation particulars in RESA. No separate filing is needed; the publication certificate becomes downloadable via lbr.lu and should be archived for banking, tax and counterparty due diligence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and publication token from LBR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains typographical errors, request correction through the LBR customer desk; rectification is published as an additional notice and becomes effective retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT and Direct Tax Registration (Tax Matriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – via Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaration of existence (form 102 for VAT and tax matriculation) with the AEDT through MyGuichet, using the RCS matricule. Obtain the Luxembourg VAT number for the SCSp (tax-transparent for income tax, but generally a separate taxable person for VAT). If no taxable turnover in Luxembourg is expected, apply for a group VAT or exemption status. The ACD will attribute a direct tax file to the partners.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and matricule
Partnership agreement
Identity documents of the general partner and gérant
Registered office proof
Bank account details (IBAN) after account opening
Estimated turnover and activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests clarifications on VAT thresholds, file a supplementary statement within 15 days; late registration penalties can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure and by demonstrating good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Registration (Employer and Self-Employed Status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg – online portal secu.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp will hire staff, register the partnership as an employer with CCSS before the first salary payment and enter into the statutory health/pension scheme. If the general partner or gérant is a natural person, register them as self-employed/salaried for social security purposes. Submit employment declarations through the CCSS portal.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Partnership agreement and management provisions
Identity of the gérant and future employees
Employment contracts or mandate documents
Date of first business operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is late, contact CCSS immediately to effect retroactive affiliation and negotiate a payment plan for unpaid social contributions; appeal an assessment within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verification of Establishment Permit Requirement (Industrial & Physical Licensing Check)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale PME (autorisation d'établissement) via Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Screen the planned no-code software activity against the regulated professions list of the amended Law of 2 September 2011. ISIC 6201 software/application building is not a regulated profession; therefore no autorisation d'établissement, state operating license, or industrial permit is required. If premises are leased, confirm municipal fire and zoning compliance; keep on file the RCS extract, the activity description and the lease contract to prove lawful operations.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Business activity description (no-code visual site builder under ISIC 6201)
Lease agreement for Luxembourg office/domiciliation
Identity of the general partner and gérant
Evidence that the activity is not listed as regulated (Ministry's profession list)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry concludes that an establishment permit is nevertheless required, file an application for authorisation d'établissement with supporting diplomas/certificates within 15 days and abstain from regulated acts pending issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale PME (Autorisation d'établissement / Regulated Professions List)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating licence or industrial permit required for ISIC 6201 (no-code visual web application builder); the RCS registration, VAT number and municipal zoning compliance suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure office/SaaS activity with no industrial installation; no EIA report, no environmental registration, and no preliminary enquiry required under the amended Law of 22 May 2008 on Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. Office operations must comply with Luxembourg municipal waste sorting rules, the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste prevention and management, and the general thresholds for electromagnetic/IT equipment conformity (CE, WEEE/RoHS directives); no discharge permits applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: for a standard office/IT workspace, a fire-safety attestation from the building owner or a light fire-safety certificate for offices (respecting Grand-Ducal Regulation on workplace premises) suffices; no civil defense clearance is required. Occupational clearance: comply with the labour code and the Law of 17 June 1994 on occupational health and safety, including electrical safety, work equipment testing, first-aid provisions, and fire escape plans; no special structural load inspection applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate and personal income tax matters. The statutory registration and filing portal is MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu, operated by the Luxembourg government in cooperation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the RCS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Luxembourg that makes taxable supplies or holds a Luxembourg fixed establishment must apply to the AEDT for VAT registration before the first taxable transaction. EU-established entities register directly through MyGuichet.lu using authenticated electronic identity; non-EU-established entities are required to appoint an accredited VAT fiscal representative. The application consists of the official VAT registration form, constitutional documents, proof of the beneficial owners and directors, the registered office address, and, for the SCSp, the RCS extraction confirming the registered partnership. Upon completion, the AEDT issues the Luxembourg national identification number (matricule) and a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU00000000. The same matricule is used by the ACD for direct tax purposes, and no separate direct-tax enrollment is required for a fiscally transparent SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. An SCSp is by law classified as fiscally transparent for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax purposes, while it constitutes a taxable person for VAT purposes. No statutory election allows the SCSp to opt into entity-level corporate income taxation. However, taxpayers may request an advance tax ruling from the Luxembourg tax authorities to confirm the transparency classification and to determine any hybrid mismatch consequence under the ATAD rules where another jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law, implementing the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises under the domestic small-business exemption; non-established taxable persons have no threshold and registration is mandatory from the first Luxembourg taxable supply, subject to EU schemes for distance sales and OSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based continuous transaction controls, and no digital stamping requirement for B2B or B2C invoices. Electronic invoicing is voluntary in the private sector unless contractually agreed. Invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector entities are subject to mandatory e-invoicing through the national electronic invoicing infrastructure based on the PEPPOL interoperability framework. All taxable persons remain subject to the standard VAT invoicing conditions under Luxembourg VAT law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for zero-rated export VAT provided the exporter holds contemporaneous proof of physical dispatch or transport out of the EU within the deadlines specified in the Luxembourg VAT Law. Intra-Community supplies to a EU VAT-registered customer are zero-rated under the conditions of Article 43 of the VAT Directive, as transposed, requiring the customer's valid VAT number and EC Sales List reporting. For digital and SaaS services such as low-code website builder subscriptions, supplies to a non-EU business customer are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT or zero-rated as B2B services under the place-of-supply rules where the customer is established outside the EU and the recipient is a taxable person. Where the non-EU customer is a private consumer, the supply falls outside Luxembourg VAT, but is not classified as an export zero-rating event. Input VAT deduction on costs attributed to zero-rated exports is permitted if the same export substantiation file is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export declaration in the ECS system / Single Administrative Document) for physical goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or other transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate and corresponding bank statements supporting the FX repatriation of export proceeds
Commercial Invoice matching the VAT invoice, together with the export contract or purchase order
Proof of dispatch from warehouse including packing lists, shipping instructions and inventory records
Customer VAT identification number for intra-Community zero-rating; for non-EU B2B services, evidence of the customer's business status and establishment jurisdiction
Declaration of value, origin, and any export license or permit where required under EU customs law
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict ex-post audit by the AEDT and Luxembourg customs authorities. Missing, incomplete or late export evidence causes the zero rate to be denied, resulting in reassessment at the standard 17% VAT rate plus late payment interest. Fabricating export declarations, issuing false bills of lading, or knowingly submitting fraudulent documentation triggers clawback of all VAT avoided, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud, VAT evasion and forgery. The AEDT and the Public Prosecutor may also impose monetary penalties proportionate to the tax evaded, and limitation periods are extended in cases of fraud or wilful evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting together with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for bank licensing, AML/CTF supervision, and payment-system oversight. The BCL does not operate a discretionary foreign-exchange permit regime; Luxembourg is bound by EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has complete convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange-control approvals, no currency quota, and no profit-repatriation licensing. For an SCSp governed by the Luxembourg law of 2013 on special limited partnerships, profit distributions follow the partnership agreement and are generally paid without entity-level Luxembourg withholding tax where the SCSp is tax-transparent for Luxembourg purposes. Residual barriers are limited to standard AML/KYC onboarding, EU/UN sanctions screening, and fiscal documentation obligations (FATCA/CRS). No de facto restriction applies to a no-code software seller collecting USD, EUR, or other currencies from global sub-sellers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory surrender requirement, holding-period obligation, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Foreign-currency receipts may be credited directly to an SCSp foreign-currency accounts without BCL approval or forced conversion to EUR. The SCSp may retain USD balances, sell them via a forward, or convert them on the spot market. The only Treasury requirement is evidentiary documentation for the underlying software service transaction under EU Regulation 2015/847 and the Luxembourg AML/CTF law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
Bank of China (Europe) S.A. Luxembourg Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary payment rail, Low as the primary treasury or escrow banking layer. Luxembourg-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and EU-authorized digital banks passporting under PSD2 can process SaaS subscription pay-ins through Stripe/Paddle, issue IBANs, and support low-value disbursements. However, offshore non-EU digital EMIs are not permissible as the core corporate bank for a Luxembourg SCSp because they lack a full EU credit-institution licence and cannot safely escrow partnership capital contributions or support trade-clearing services. The feasible model is to use an EU-licensed EMI solely for collection/disbursement automation and settle net balances daily to a BCL-supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML legislation and CSSF circulars permit remote identification through compliant video-identification and digital signature solutions; there is no absolute statutory requirement for directors to attend a physical bank visit. In practice, however, Luxembourg relationship banks commonly require at least one in-person compliance interview at the Luxembourg registered office for cross-border SCSp structures with foreign limited partners or non-EU ultimate beneficial owners. Remote account opening is viable where all UBOs are natural persons resident in EU/EEA and the SCSp has a low-risk no-code software business, but the safest approval path is one physical meeting in Luxembourg plus authenticated board resolutions designating bank signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank is unable to identify each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner of the SCSp through the GP, the partnership agreement, and the LP interest register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SCSp partnership agreement; updated LP register; shareholding/organizational chart showing the natural-person control chain; GP certificate of good standing; passport pages and proof of address for every UBO holding more than 25% or exercising effective control; a formal legal opinion confirming the partnership’s ownership structure under Luxembourg law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU limited partners or beneficiaries resident in high-risk third-country jurisdictions trigger enhanced due diligence and possible rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement and source-of-funds evidence; notarized ID documents and apostilled corporate records; professional bank reference letters on bank letterhead; explanation of the LP investment purpose; evidence that the transferred capital derives from lawful software-engineering or investment activities and does not create money-laundering or sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The no-code SaaS business uses Stripe/Paddle volumes that the bank may associate with high refunds, chargebacks, or third-party sub-seller flows requiring payment-settlement licensing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard Terms of Service; customer contracts; privacy policy; detailed product-and-revenue model showing that payments are for non-financial digital-service subscriptions; transaction-flow diagrams from Stripe/Paddle to the Luxembourg bank account; a legal opinion that the activity is not a regulated payment service and that the SCSp is itself the merchant receiving settlement funds, not an intermediary holding third-party money.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately large cross-border capital contributions or rapid outbound disbursements relative to expected SaaS revenue are flagged as potential pass-through or shadow-banking activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SCSp cash-flow forecast and treasury policy; capital contribution agreements from LPs; underlying commercial contracts for the no-code platform subscriptions/revenue sharing; invoices or disbursement schedules for outbound vendor payments; monthly projected balance sheet and tax accounts of the SCSp; senior-manager attestation explaining the economic purpose of large flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners or family members are identified as politically exposed persons (PEPs), or the ownership chain contains a discretionary trust or foundation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP status declaration by each UBO; source-of-funds evidence covering all materials entering the SCSp account; substantive consolidation of trust/foundation constitutional documents; independent legal advice confirming actual ownership and control; ongoing notification commitment to the compliance officer; verified structure chart and a description of each intermediate entity’s operating substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions to the Luxembourg SCSp must be routed through a licensed EU credit institution using SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR wires. No BCL approval or exchange-control permit is required. The compliant protocol requires the full SCSp legal name as beneficiary in MT103 field 59, a clear beneficiary IBAN, and a purpose description in field 70 including the words 'Capital contribution to SCSp' or 'Subcription payment in accordance with partnership agreement'. The sending bank must provide the investor’s full name, address, and account number pursuant to EU Regulation 2015/847. For USD or multi-currency inflows, the bank may use a correspondent clearing path; the SCSp may either hold the foreign currency or convert it by spot/forward transaction. To avoid onboarding delays, every inbound capital wire must be supported by the SCSp capital contribution agreement, an updated LP list, and an UBO identification pack lodged with the bank before the first payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For normal operating disbursements, the primary clearing rails are SEPA Instant/SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR and SWIFT MT103 for USD/GBP/CHF/JPY. The SCSp may pass through the Stripe/Paddle platform for receiving SaaS subscription revenue; subsequent vendor payments for cloud infrastructure, contractors, or third-party software tools are executed by a bank-originated wire. A commercial documentary credit (SWIFT MT700) is permissible for large cross-border procurement of hardware/licensed infrastructure where an irrevocable letter of credit is contractually required, although pure no-code software services usually settle by MT103. For avoidable concentration risk, the SCSp should maintain two MT103-capable correspondent bank accounts in Luxembourg/EU and apply matching discipline for USD cashflow receipts and disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards between the SCSp and a Luxembourg/EU bank under an ISDA or local master agreement, for hedging USD/CHF/GBP receipts into EUR
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-market-convertible emerging-market currencies that arise from software exports
Cross-Currency Swaps to match long-dated capital contributions or multi-currency liquidity positions
Vanilla FX Options purchased to establish a maximum EUR conversion cost without removing upside

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year, regardless of financial year-end; updates arising from ownership changes are filed within one month from event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 750-5,000 (approx. USD 815-5,400) for late confirmation; wilful or repeated non-compliance may incur criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and/or temporary suspension of RCS extracts; no automatic strike-off, but persistent refusal can lead to court-ordered enforcement by the public prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing - only when statutory publication thresholds are exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS); published in the RESA (electronic gazette)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after close of the financial year (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end); no official extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the general partner to a coercive court order with periodic penalty payment (astreinte), criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 (approx. USD 27,000), and administrative publication of non-compliance; continued default may ultimately result in judicial winding-up and deletion from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is required if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three Luxembourg thresholds: total balance sheet > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average workforce > 50. Audit is also compulsory for parent companies preparing consolidated accounts or where the SCSp is itself a financial undertaking; otherwise small and mid-size SCSp are exempt from both audit and publication.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of commercial companies, as amended) transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for certain entities (e.g., credit institutions and listed undertakings). The general partner must maintain accounting records consistent with the Luxembourg plan comptable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SCSp is required to confirm its beneficial owner register at least once per calendar year between 1 January and 31 March online through the LBR portal. Any transfer of partnership interests resulting in direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or control of the partnership by other means, must be filed as an RBE update within one month after the change comes to the general partner's knowledge. The annual confirmation must restate all existing beneficial owners or certify that there has been no change; failure to file a timely confirmation is a separate contravention from failure to update ownership changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners / Managers (Registre des gerants)
Minute Book of Partners' Decisions (Registre des proces-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - 4,500 per year for a compliant Luxembourg registered office/agent service (including RBE confirmation assistance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 25,000 per engagement when statutory audit is triggered; typically USD 0 for exempt small SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate for Luxembourg City (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 1.19% + municipal business tax 6.75%); an SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself an RC taxpayer where pass-through treatment applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains from foreign subsidiaries (holding threshold 10% or acquisition cost of EUR 6 million). No general IP box exists for new no-code/digital platform intangibles; ordinary subscription revenue from visual web template and low-code SaaS sales is taxed as standard commercial income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Luxembourg corporate income tax return) / Form 1001 (municipal business tax return) filed electronically via MyGuichet and the ACD (Administration des contributions directes) e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional tax prepayments on account are required for taxable corporate partners and for any SCSp that loses pass-through eligibility.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 December of the following year. For non-calendar year-ends, the return is due no later than 12 months after the fiscal year-end unless the ACD grants an extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), tax ID (TIN), legal form (SCSp), general partner details, and business address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must provide a Luxembourg tax number and an authorised Luxembourg tax representative or general partner; if the SCSp is managed abroad, state the place of effective management and attach supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Commercial income, operating expenses, and net taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Global taxable turnover as allocated under Luxembourg GAAP, less substantiated operating costs, depreciation, provisions, and deductions; no-code platform subscription revenue must be included in ordinary turnover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner may only report Luxembourg-source income actually allocated by the SCSp; worldwide revenue is excluded unless the partner carries on a Luxembourg permanent establishment through the SCSp.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption claims, dividend relief, capital gains relief, foreign tax credits, and treaty residence positions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a current tax residence certificate (TRC), ownership schedule, and a declaration of effective active business conduct to support treaty benefits; a mere legal owner without substance will not qualify.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border transactions with related parties, pricing methods used, and the file reference of the Local File/Master File.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with cross-border related-party sales, royalties, or service fees above the Luxembourg TP threshold must attach the Local File and identify the Master File provider; failure to complete Box 4 triggers automatic documentation penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on assessed tax, monthly arrears interest of 0.8%, ex officio assessment, and administrative fines up to EUR 1,000 per missing or incorrect declaration. Fraudulent non-filing escalates to criminal tax penalties and possible imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp fiscal transparency return and partner information schedule (informational annex to Form 1000 or standalone pass-through allocation statement) filed through the ACD/MyGuichet online channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, coinciding with the SCSp fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The transparency allocation statement must be filed by 31 December following the fiscal year-end; partner allocation schedules must be issued before the partners' own tax return deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, tax residence, share class, profit sharing percentage, and allocated taxable income or loss for each SCSp partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide their country TIN and confirm whether Luxembourg-source allocations are taxable in Luxembourg under their residence treaty. The SCSp must not issue a K-1 style allocation for a partner who fails beneficial ownership identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contributions, withdrawals, profit distributions, and reallocations during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions that are not supported by actual economic participation are recharacterized as employment income, director fees, or dividends and trigger withholding tax, payroll tax, or treaty limitation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the partner allocation schedule is treated as an incorrect declaration under Article 176 LIR: a EUR 1,000 administrative fine, loss of pass-through filing priority, and potential criminal penalty for concealment of beneficial ownership.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces the rate to 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders, and applicable DTAs may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 15%. A fiscally transparent SCSp pays no dividend withholding tax at partnership level; profit allocations are taxed at partner level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the taxpayer must file a withholding tax relief or refund application with the ACD. Required items include a valid TRC from the residence state, evidence of beneficial ownership within 12 months, ownership/parking statements, and a declaration that the structure was not designed mainly to obtain the treaty benefit. Relief at source is granted only after substance review; otherwise a refund claim must be made within five years from the calendar year of the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalty payments, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner with real functions, assets, and risks. Interest: 0% withholding tax on arm's-length interest paid to non-residents. Excess or artificially classed interest is reconstructed as a dividend and becomes subject to 15% dividend withholding tax under Luxembourg thin capitalisation/GAAR rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10 million annual cross-border related-party turnover (gross intragroup revenue, royalty streams, and service fees) triggers the mandatory Luxembourg Local File. A group Master File is required where worldwide consolidated revenue of the group exceeds EUR 750 million and the Luxembourg entity carries out related-party transactions. CbC reporting notification applies at the same EUR 750 million group threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not legislatively label an ESR rule, but economic substance is imposed through GAAR, Article 56 LIR, the ATAD principal-purpose test, the OECD MLI, and Luxembourg Anti-Abuse Law. An SCSp must show local administrative substance: real physical premises, local employees, executive decision-making by the general partner, separate bank accounts, financial statements, and minutes. A transparent structure without local substance will be recharacterised as a Luxembourg tax resident corporate vehicle or denied treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Failure to Declare Digital Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing no-code website builder subscription revenues from Stripe/Paddle away from the SCSp's books, issuing no invoices, treating recurring SaaS income as tax-free capital, or deliberately understating turnover in the Luxembourg return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of omitted income at the aggregate 24.94% CIT/municipal rate applicable to a corporate partner, 10% late-filing surcharge, 0.8% monthly arrears interest, and criminal fraud penalties including fines up to ten times the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the SCSp and any de facto manager who signs a false return is jointly liable for unpaid taxes, penalties, and interest. Courts may pierce the partnership veil to issue travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment where evasion is linked to money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abuse of SCSp Fiscally Transparent Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SCSp with no premises, employees, bank account, or managerial substance merely to channel software royalties or SaaS profits to offshore partners in zero-tax jurisdictions, without meeting Luxembourg GAAR and ATAD substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD disregards the pass-through personality and taxes the SCSp as a resident company: 24.94% CIT on worldwide commercial income, 0.5% net wealth tax where applicable, municipal business tax, and 15% dividend withholding tax on distributions; DTA benefits are denied and penalty interest applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is personally liable on the SCSp's obligations when the structure is a sham. Nominee partners and professional directors who facilitate the shell arrangement face civil restitution, disqualification from Luxembourg management, travel restrictions, and criminal sanctions under AML law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling software licenses, platform services, or marketing support to a related Hong Kong, Cayman, or U.S. affiliate at zero or non-arm's-length margins, leaving all profit outside Luxembourg while the SCSp bears development, hosting, payment, and legal risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg Article 56 LIR re-amends income to the arm's-length result; the shortfall is taxed at 24.94% plus default interest of 0.8% per month. A 50% to 100% negligence penalty is added where documentation is absent, fabricated, or contradictory; excess balances may be reclassified as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length contracts without obtaining comparables are personally liable for the additional corporate tax. Fabrication of TP documentation exposes the signing manager to criminal punishment and personal liability, including disqualification from board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Profit Extraction and Withholding Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating profit as excessive shareholder loans, inflated interest, informal founder drawings, or tax-free SCSp distributions to a taxable corporate partner, while failing to withhold 15% dividend tax where Luxembourg law treats the payment as a dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The excess interest or distribution is recharacterised as a dividend, attracting 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, a 10% failure-to-withhold penalty, and monthly interest of 0.8%. In fraud cases the responsible officer faces imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and general partner are personally liable for uncollected withholding taxes and penalties. Non-resident founders who knowingly misuse shareholder loans can be held personally liable and subjected to a Luxembourg anti-abuse investigation, with travel bans and asset seizures where the payment is traced to shell entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/Beneficial Ownership Failure and Payment Rail Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration in Luxembourg's RBE register; concealing the real developer/founder behind anonymous nominees; directing Stripe/Paddle payments to foreign bank accounts of creditors in high-risk jurisdictions; ignoring discrepancies between the disclosed partner and actual recipient of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to EUR 1.25 million or 10% of annual turnover for AML failings; individual directors face fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for false RBE filings. The beneficial ownership statement may be suspended and enforced through criminal seizure of payment-system claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot rely on the SCSp shield: the general partner and every manager who fails AML/KYC obligations is personally liable for fines, restoration of misused funds, travel restraints, and criminal prison sentences. Once AML liability attaches, the tax administration and public prosecutor can pierce all corporate and partnership layers to recover funds.
